Gary Player. The Black Knight, named for his signature black attire. A South African professional golfer who won 9 major championships and became the first player from the Southern Hemisphere to achieve dominance in international golf. His global prominence, competitive longevity, and emphasis on fitness transformed professional golf.

He won 9 major championships: 3 Masters in 1961, 1974, and 1978, 3 PGA Championships in 1962, 1972, and 1978, 2 Open Championships in 1959 and 1968, and 1 US Open in 1965. He achieved the Career Grand Slam—winning all four major championships—in 1965, the third player to do so at that time. Player won tournaments on six continents, establishing himself as the first truly global golf figure. He was known for his extraordinary physical fitness and dedication to exercise, pioneering the athlete-as-fitness-model approach decades before it became standard.

He competed professionally across multiple decades, winning a senior major championship at age 48. He won 23 PGA Tour events and numerous international tournaments, establishing himself as a worldwide ambassador for the sport. Player broke down racial and geographic barriers in professional golf, representing South Africa during the apartheid era while becoming an international star. Jack Nicklaus was a contemporary rival throughout the 1960s and 1970s, Arnold Palmer was a fellow competitor from the same era, and Tom Watson was a younger competitor who overlapped with Player's career.
